name: manual_549189
claim: A non-empty diff and a matching parent/child tree delta prove that SOME content changed at a destination -- they do not prove the INTENDED artifact reached it. This is a real, distinct gap from (and one step beyond) the earlier empty-commit lesson (lesson_fee9305e811e, extending lesson_9fac191b11e1): even when a commit's tree genuinely differs from its parent (ruling out the empty-commit failure mode already documented), the diff could still be the WRONG content -- a stale cached version, a different file entirely, a partial write -- and "the tree changed" alone would not catch it. Confirmed via a real review finding on orama-system PR #339 (pullrequestreview-5095683687): the existing mandatory git-publication-verification sequence in bin/orama-system/afrp/failure-modes.md stopped at `git show --stat --oneline HEAD` (confirms a non-empty diff exists) and the equivalent AFRP SKILL.md proxy-table row stopped at "compare parent/child trees" -- both insufficient by the review's own precise framing. Fixed by adding a mandatory final verification step to both: `git show HEAD:<path> | grep -q "<expected-marker>"`, confirming the SPECIFIC intended content (a distinctive string, section heading, or function signature -- not a generic pattern that would also match unrelated content) is actually present in the committed blob, not just that some diff occurred. Verified the exact command pattern both directions (matches a real marker; correctly reports absence for a fabricated one) before writing it into the docs, rather than assuming the pattern would work. General, reusable rule for any content-publication workflow, not specific to git: after every write operation, verify the actual destination contains the specific expected content marker, not merely that the write "succeeded" or that some observable signal (HTTP 200, new SHA, non-empty diff, changed byte count) occurred -- those are all transport evidence, not content evidence. Caught and fixed a real inaccuracy in my own first draft of the doc explanation before committing: initially described a specific commit as having "a different parent but wrong content," when its actual documented defect was a zero tree delta from its real parent -- a materially different claim; corrected by rereading my own addition critically before pushing, not because it was flagged by someone else.

decisions.notes: A real, distinct verification-discipline gap found via direct review on orama-system PR #339, fixed in both afrp/failure-modes.md and afrp/SKILL.md this session -- generalizes beyond git to any content-publication workflow.
